## Abstract {.unnumbered}

Accurate progesterone receptor (PR) status is a critical determinant of endocrine therapy eligibility in breast cancer, yet standard immunohistochemistry (IHC) exhibits substantial inter-pathologist variability in diagnostically ambiguous cases. While pathology images alone often lack the molecular context required to resolve these ambiguous receptor states, traditional late-fusion models struggle to align coarse genomic profiles with gigapixel images. 

To bridge this gap, we present a multimodal clinical decision-support system that integrates RNA-Seq transcriptomic profiles with whole-slide imaging (WSI). We introduce an asymmetric cross-attention mechanism in which the patient's transcriptomic profile guides visual evidence retrieval from the tissue image with linear computational complexity. To ensure safety in clinical deployment, a Cross-Modal Reliability Estimator provides a calibrated per-patient confidence score, automating the escalation of ambiguous or discordant cases to pathologist review. Furthermore, we introduce a normalization-corrected Top-1%-Mass Concentration metric that quantifies attentional focus consistently across slides of any size.

Using the TCGA-BRCA cohort of 951 patients with matched molecular and imaging data, the model achieved an ROC-AUC of 0.8482 and PR-AUC of 0.9054. Analysis of attention patterns revealed significant phenotypic separation between PR-positive and PR-negative tumors (p = 0.018), confirming that the model captures spatial patterns associated with distinct PR phenotypes. 

Together, these findings demonstrate that genomic-conditioned visual search is an effective framework for clinical decision support in computational pathology, proving that rigorous measurement design is key to unlocking complex biological signals.

## Key Contributions & Findings {.unnumbered}

::: {.contributions}
- **Asymmetric Cross-Attention Architecture:** Developed an efficient $O(N)$ framework where genomic conditioning occurs at the visual search stage before slide-level compression, yielding a +0.0801 ROC-AUC gain over late-fusion baselines.
- **Calibrated Clinical Safety Gate:** Implemented a Cross-Modal Reliability Estimator that computes per-patient confidence scores to automatically flag and escalate uncertain cases for expert human review.
- **Size-Invariant Interpretability:** Designed a normalization-corrected concentration metric that overcomes slide-size confounders, revealing emergent biological grounding through statistically robust phenotypic attention separation (p = 0.018).
:::

## Limitations {.unnumbered}
::: {.contributions}
- **Single-Cohort Validation:** Trained and evaluated exclusively on the TCGA-BRCA cohort; out-of-distribution performance across diverse acquisition platforms and staining protocols remains uncharacterized.
- **Assay & Data Availability:** Relies on matched whole-transcriptome RNA-Seq data, which involves higher turnaround times and costs compared to standard standalone IHC or H&E workflows in routine clinical practice.
- **Vision Encoder Alignment:** The current vision encoder is pretrained on pathology images alone, limiting cross-modal reliability. Fine-tuning on joint data or adopting a transcriptomics-guided encoder represents the primary path forward.
:::
